speaking.q: Can information that seems harmless on its own become dangerous when it is combined with other pieces of information?
If someone had access to several months of your location history, how much could they learn about your private life?
When we click “accept” on a website or app, can we really say that we have freely agreed to what will happen to our personal information?
Should people be able to prevent old information from appearing in search results, or does the public have a right to access the past?
Do all people have the same ability to protect their privacy, or are some groups much more vulnerable than others?
Many technologies make our lives easier by collecting personal information. At what point does convenience stop being worth the loss of privacy?
Are there situations in which the public's right to information should be more important than an individual's right to privacy?
If complete privacy is impossible in modern life, what would a realistic and responsible approach to digital privacy look like?
